newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Gold closes higher in two-way Hong Kong trade.
newsitem.headline: Gold closes higher in two-way Hong Kong trade.

text.p: Hong Kong gold closed higher on Thursday after a day of two-way trading following an overnight fall in New York, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$347.60/348.10 an ounce against New York's US$346.80/347.30 close on Wednesday and Hong Kong's previous close of US$349.20/70.
"Gold came under pressure today following German newspaper reports of gold sales by Germany, but the U.S. dollar's dip against the yen should provide support," a local trading house dealer said.
"The immediate gold trend is uncertain and I think gold will stay range-bound, with support at US$345 and resistance at US$350," a bullion dealer said.
Local gold ended HK$13 lower at HK$3,213 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to nil from its previous fix at -5.00.
